boundary: which allocator owns the object the defect touches: pymalloc (nested) or libc malloc (non-nested). Decided per case by MEASUREMENT, not by the object's size -- the ASan heap report is run twice and the question is whether it SURVIVES PYTHONMALLOC=pymalloc
title: CPython 3.13.7 spatial defects at the pymalloc boundary, plus temporal and spatial defects whose memory comes straight from libc malloc
note: A sibling of pymalloc-repros. That corpus is scoped to consumer-side TEMPORAL defects whose memory comes from pymalloc and asserts completeness for that cell (20 cases, expect_live_in_pin {true: 20}, a shape_prose regex on "[Tt]wenty reports"), so cases here were not added there. 32 cases from 31 upstream fixes (03 and 04 are two triggers for gh-140492). Cases 01-21 are the three cells pymalloc-repros does not cover: 13 spatial/nested, 5 spatial/non-nested, 3 temporal/non-nested. Cases 22-32 are 11 temporal/nested defects, the same upstream issues pymalloc-repros holds as C models (each carries a sibling_issue pointer), here because a C model and an interpreter run of one defect are not the same measurement -- on the base arm the C models all complete while three of the eleven fault, all with cause 24; the two corpora's numbers must not be pooled. Liveness and the nested/non-nested side are both measured on the pinned ASan build. The Capstone arms are virtual-malloc and virtual-nested-pools on the virtual profile, where CPython's one heap is musl mallocng: pymalloc stock, and pymalloc on its lifetime port (tools/arms.json virtual-cpython, virtual-cpython-pools). Their faults are attributed through fault_sites from a host ASan run (results/2026-10-10-asan). The physical arms spatial and sublet (level0 heap) measured 2026-10-06 to 2026-10-09 are superseded; their record stays in results/20261006, whose tables probe/counts.py derives. results/20261006/ also carries the negative controls measured on the physical arms: a weak one that passes on all three, and a strong per-case one (negative_control.py, 18 of the 32 cases), run on the base arm; what each settles and what neither does is in that README. Neither has been run on the virtual arms yet.
